paragraphs: Direct assessment: If you are willing to ask questions about disease and health, repeatedly check methods and data, and report limitations honestly, explore further. The safe trial uses only this page's four entirely fictional rows of numbers. Public or de-identified data do not automatically carry research permission.

Observe behavior: Can you retain original values, recalculate, and acknowledge unknown conditions? Actual research also requires training, supervisor feedback, and institutional permissions. This exercise checks only one paper assignment.

Continue if you are willing to train over the long term and accept challenges to methods. If you are unwilling to check data or face uncertain conclusions, first compare methods, coordination, or engineering directions. Interest is neither hiring nor permission.

60-minute paper exercise (editor-created fiction): Four nonrandom observational records A1: X=1, Y=3; A2: X=3, Y=7; B1: X=1, Y=2; B2: X=3, Y=4. X and Y are unitless, not patients, samples, or clinical measures. Calculate the two groups' mean Y and mean difference A minus B, and decide whether you can state that A causes Y to rise. Retain original values and calculations, two limitations, and required additional design information. There are no missing values; do not collect data or calculate significance or power. Reference answer: A mean (3+7)/2=5, B mean (2+4)/2=3, A minus B=2. Only these four fictional records can be described. Grouping is nonrandom, each group has only 2 records, and sampling, temporal order, and confounding are unspecified; causation, efficacy, and significance cannot be established. Request grouping rules, measurement meanings, and study design without inventing conditions. Spend 10 minutes reading, 20 minutes calculating, 20 minutes writing limitations and requests, and 10 minutes recalculating with the answer hidden and recording corrections.

entries: Research design: Disease and health research.
Data analysis: Interpret results and write reports.

paragraphs: This page's exact scope is O*NET 19-1042.00: Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists, conducting research to understand human disease and improve health, including clinical investigations, research, and development. Epidemiologists 19-1041 are listed separately. This is a statistical classification and does not mean this occupation never studies disease transmission or population data.

O*NET 19-1042 work-context response percentages from separate questions: 94% use email daily, 84% have face-to-face discussions daily, 89% rate teamwork as extremely important, 57% rate accuracy as extremely important, 59% have some decision-making freedom, 48% typically work more than 40 hours weekly, and 47% face time pressure monthly rather than weekly. Different questions are not added together; these are neither accident rates nor a Chinese survey. BLS describes office / laboratory work, typically full time, with some working more than 40 hours.
Check methods, retain original values, and state limitations; check training and permissions separately.
Information inputs: Official 19-1042 tasks / context / IR/JobZone5 and 2025 wages. Display O*NET2024–2034 and BLS2025–2035 projections separately; do not mix periods.
Research questions, lawful data, and methods; the teaching exercise uses fictional numbers only.

Outputs include protocols, data quality and analysis versions, reproducible materials, papers, and limitation statements. If a project requires preregistration or review, retain those records separately. Do not describe a teaching draft as approved.

This page supports career exploration only. A research degree does not automatically confer clinical, sign-off, or research approval authority. Research-focused work typically requires no licensure or certification, while actual medical practice or treatment of trial patients requires appropriate medical licensure. Verify real activities against jurisdiction, institution, materials, and funding conditions.
Compare research, coordination, nursing information systems, and engineering design by actual tasks. Similar names do not imply mutual recognition of permissions.

Comparisons use current official occupational definitions; directional advice is editorial synthesis. CRCs may plan, direct, coordinate projects, and analyze data, rather than categorically having no involvement in design.

CRCs focus on achieving clinical project objectives under protocols; medical scientists focus on disease and health research. Duties may overlap, with specific permissions depending on the project and institution.

Bioengineers / biomedical engineers 17-2031 apply engineering, biological, and other principles to design, develop, and evaluate health systems / products. They also conduct research and analysis; this is not simply equipment repair.

19-1041 studies the distribution / determinants of population health events; this page's 19-1042 is another statistical scope. Classification does not establish that this occupation never uses population data.

Interpretation risks: The four exercise records support descriptions of 5 / 3 / difference 2 only, not causation, significance, or efficacy. Actual results require separate design checks.

Handle real materials through institutional safety procedures; this page does not direct isolation or operations. It presents advisory best practices, not regulations, emphasizing procedure-specific risk assessment. This round read the overview and foreword, not the full text. Institutional professionals confirm actual facilities, materials, and protection under applicable rules. The exercise involves no sampling, culture, or biological material handling.

Recruitment checklist (editorial suggestion, without a representative sample of current vacancies): The academic, hospital, and industry settings below support checking real positions individually, not job survey conclusions.
Academic setting checks: Field, methods training, paper contributions, funding, and reproducible materials. Actual requirements follow the real position.
Hospital research checks: Research duties, actual clinical actions and relevant licensure, and authorized institutional processes. A degree does not automatically permit medical practice.
Industrial R&D checks: Research milestones, methodological deliverables, collaboration, and data permissions. Do not infer universal hiring requirements from the setting.

Advancement rests on reviewable design, data, publication, and compliance records, not a guaranteed number of years.

questions.answer: 60-minute paper exercise (editor-created fiction): Four nonrandom observational records A1: X=1, Y=3; A2: X=3, Y=7; B1: X=1, Y=2; B2: X=3, Y=4. X and Y are unitless, not patients, samples, or clinical measures. Calculate the two groups' mean Y and mean difference A minus B, and decide whether you can state that A causes Y to rise. Retain original values and calculations, two limitations, and required additional design information. There are no missing values; do not collect data or calculate significance or power.
questions.question: How should I begin?

questions.answer: Reference answer: A mean (3+7)/2=5, B mean (2+4)/2=3, A minus B=2. Only these four fictional records can be described. Grouping is nonrandom, each group has only 2 records, and sampling, temporal order, and confounding are unspecified; causation, efficacy, and significance cannot be established. Request grouping rules, measurement meanings, and study design without inventing conditions. Spend 10 minutes reading, 20 minutes calculating, 20 minutes writing limitations and requests, and 10 minutes recalculating with the answer hidden and recording corrections.

components.work_context_block: O*NET 19-1042 work-context response percentages from separate questions: 94% use email daily, 84% have face-to-face discussions daily, 89% rate teamwork as extremely important, 57% rate accuracy as extremely important, 59% have some decision-making freedom, 48% typically work more than 40 hours weekly, and 47% face time pressure monthly rather than weekly. Different questions are not added together; these are neither accident rates nor a Chinese survey. BLS describes office / laboratory work, typically full time, with some working more than 40 hours. Assess capabilities through observable evidence: Form testable questions, explain design and statistical assumptions, retain data and analysis versions, distinguish correlation from causation, and communicate limitations. Verify research training and institutional permissions separately; personality labels or accuracy on this exercise do not predict competence. Full duties: Research design and execution: Form testable hypotheses, design and conduct experiments, clinical investigations, or R&D activities, and collect biomedical data while controlling quality. Analysis and outputs: Analyze data, interpret research findings, and write papers and reports. Record quality, ethics, and sharing conditions by research type and applicable rules; do not describe correlation as causation.
